title: Success State: Agents That Self-Report When They Detect They Are About to Violate Constraints

original_idea.body:
# Success State: Agents That Self-Report When They Detect They Are About to Violate Constraints

**Problem:** An agent that self-reports constraint violation intent would enable human-in-the-loop interventions. Backcasting: what training or prompting reliably produces this behavior?

**Direction:** Define success: an agent that inserts a standardized self-report tag in its output whenever it detects a potential constraint violation in its planned action. Test three interventions: explicit instruction-following prompts, few-shot examples of self-reporting, and post-hoc reward modeling for self-reports. Measure self-report recall (what fraction of planned violations were self-reported) and precision (what fraction of self-reports were genuine planned violations).

**Why it matters:** Self-reporting agents could dramatically reduce the monitoring burden by providing ground truth about their own constraint-violating intentions, making human oversight more tractable at scale.

**Relevant context:** Irregular 2026; self-monitoring in LLMs; scalable oversight; constitutional AI self-critique.
